where: data/conditions.xlsx, the Heedless row's Automation cell; printed in foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md (0.37.0)
question: Since 0.37.0 a Condition's row may raise what a thing costs: [EFFECT COST: 1; IF: TRAIT(Concentrate)]. Heedless's Automation cell is still N/A, so Heedless changes nothing until the line is in the sheet.
recommendation: Type [EFFECT COST: 1; IF: TRAIT(Concentrate)] in place of the N/A, double-click sync_conditions.cmd, then run Sync content in the open world. Its Notes cell can then say that the extra action is the row's line.

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.37.0, rulings 380 to 384
question: Readings 0.37.0 makes that Mike did not rule on. 380: IF: COST(n) on a Maneuver's row reads the version of the Maneuver used, never a price a Condition raised (a Heedless creature paying 2 for a 1-action version gets the 1-action results). 381: one Condition counts once (its largest matching COST line) and two Conditions add. 382: the raise goes wherever the cost goes, so nothing outside an encounter, and Recenter pays it with the tracking setting off, as it pays its own action. 383: adversaries pay it. 384: a Maneuver whose trait is written 'Auditory or Visual' is neither trait for a cost.
recommendation: Leave them. The one to know is the reach of the word: it raises Maneuvers paid from their own row, and Recenter. Strikes, Casts, movement, Reactions and the other Maneuvers the system runs itself cost what they always cost; say if one of them should be raised too.

where: data/conditions.xlsx (Frightened); data/talents_cultures.xlsx, Serrovane (Contract Literate); data/talents_ancestries.xlsx, Human (Jack of All Trades); printed in foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md (0.36.0)
question: Since 0.36.0 a bare CHECK reaches every roll and Threshold, and SKILL is the word for checks that are no attack and no Defense. Three cells use a bare CHECK. Frightened's three lines (DEF, CHECK, ATK) were read again by the Conditions build of 2026-11-19: its CHECK line is every roll now, the numbers are the same, and the build says the DEF and ATK lines can go. Contract Literate's claimed +2 and Jack of All Trades' +1 mean the narrow scope, and keep it only until their cells are parsed again: at the next content build a cell that still says CHECK becomes an every-roll line (Contract Literate's claim would be offered on attack and Defense rolls and could be spent by a foe's attack). Sync content does not change them.
recommendation: Frightened: leave the three lines, or write the one line [EFFECT CHECK: -N condition] to quiet the build's warning; either gives the same numbers. Contract Literate: write [EFFECT SKILL: 2 condition; IF: CLAIM(noticing hidden clauses, traps or altered terms in an agreement)] BEFORE the next content build. Jack of All Trades: when its cell is written, [EFFECT SKILL: 1 situation; IF: RANK(roll = untrained)].

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.36.0, rulings 369 to 371 and 374
question: Three readings 0.36.0 makes that Mike did not rule on. 369: a line keeps the meaning it was read with, so a rule stored before 0.36.0 from a bare CHECK stays narrow until its cell is parsed again (a content build, the Conditions build, a change to the text in a world Item's Automation box, a change to a custom effect row's text or label; never by Sync content). 370: an every-roll line reaches a Defense rolled as a check (the Wind roll, a Recovery, a Search with Awareness, the default Initiative) once, through the Defense's own number; a SKILL line and a bonus to a Maneuver made without its Item still do not. 371: a claim on a bare CHECK is offered on every roll, attacks and Defense rolls included, and an armed one is spent by the next roll or Threshold read, a foe's attack among them. Also unbuilt: an every-roll line with IF: RANK(roll ...) does not reach Defenses. 374: one press of Ten minutes' rest is one stretch of ten minutes, so each press restores level x Presence Vigor and lowers Fatigued by 1 (thirty minutes are three presses), for a character and for an adversary alike.
recommendation: Leave them. The one to know is 369: Contract Literate must be rewritten with SKILL before the next content build, or its claim becomes an every-roll claim. Say so if SKILL should also reach checks rolled with a Defense's Constellation (a Search with Awareness): it does not today, as a bare CHECK did not.

where: data/conditions.xlsx, the Effect cells of Bound, Controlled, Controlling and Wrong-Footed; printed in foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md (0.35.1)
question: Since 0.35.1 [X] in a Condition's Effect is the creature the Condition is about, and the sheet's tooltip and the token's hover card print its name. The four rows that take a creature still write a bare X (or 'that creature'), so nothing is filled in yet and the build warns on three of them.
recommendation: In those four Effect cells write [X] for each X (Wrong-Footed: 'Off-Guard against [X] only.'), save, double-click sync_conditions.cmd, then run Sync content in the open world.

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.35.1, rulings 364 and 365
question: Two readings 0.35.1 makes that Mike did not rule on. 364: who [X] is. For Bound, Controlled and Controlling it is the Bind partner, and only while the creature is in that Bind (one toggled from the token by hand names nobody); for any other row that takes X it is whoever put the Condition on with a Maneuver. The name is the one the sheet already shows for that creature beside it, with no 'the' in front. 365: [X] is read in the Effect and the Description of a row whose Takes is X; anywhere else it prints as typed and the build says so; the 'that creature' fallback takes a capital where it begins a sentence.
recommendation: Leave both. Say so if the token's name should be shown in place of the sheet's (they differ for an unlinked token renamed on the map, such as 'Bandit 2').

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.35.0, rulings 356 to 360
question: Readings 0.35.0 makes that Mike did not rule on. 356 (his choice: a Condition's row only) with Claude's detail: one trait to a line, nothing after it, and IMMUNE: <Condition> stays refused on a Condition's row. 357: a thing's separate traits are alternatives for immunity (Calm Animal, Auditory and Visual, does nothing to a creature that is only Blinded), while one trait written 'Auditory or Visual' (Captivate) needs both. 358: immunity is judged when a thing would land, each card as it is posted and the write again; a reroll's card asks again; there is no override (see the row below). 359: a Condition held only against one creature gives its immunity only against that creature. 360: 'nothing lands' covers a Maneuver's target lines, a result given to an ally, an attack's damage buttons and the Expose of the defender's Zone; the roller's own lines stand; an immune defender still pays for its Reaction; a Maneuver performed as part of another carries its parent's traits; 'Trait' and 'Expose' are names a new Condition may not take.
recommendation: Leave them. The one to know is 357: Calm Animal cannot calm a Blinded animal though it is also Auditory. If a Maneuver with two separate traits should need immunity to both, write its trait as one, 'Auditory or Visual', as Captivate's is.

where: foundry/starwrought/module/documents/cards/apply.mjs, applyOnce; the 0.35.0 plan's 'There is no override'
question: While a creature has the Condition, 'Apply to <creature>' applies nothing however often it is pressed. The plan said deleting the small 'immune' card brings the button back; it does, but the press asks again and posts the same card (the review found this). So the only way to affect an immune creature by a GM's ruling is to take the Condition off, press Apply, and put it back. Should the GM have an 'Apply anyway'?
recommendation: Leave it unless play asks for it. If wanted: a GM-only 'Apply anyway' button on the small 'immune' card, which applies the lines once and says so. It is a small change in apply.mjs.

where: data/conditions.xlsx, the About sheet
question: Three sentences of the About sheet describe the sheet as it was before the Effect column: 'Description: the text players read ...' (that is Effect now; Description is the flavor line), and the Automation sentence, which lists CHECK, ATK, DEF and INIT and not IMMUNE for a trait.
recommendation: Reword when convenient; nothing reads the About sheet. Suggested wording is in the 0.35.0 changelog entry, under Worth knowing. Since 0.35.1 it also wants one sentence under Effect for [X] (the 0.35.1 changelog entry has it).

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.34.0, rulings 341 to 349
question: Readings 0.34.0 makes that Mike did not rule on. 341 (his: a typed number for each Skill) with Claude's additions: Melee and Ranged have one too, a Defense on the left of vs reads the adversary's typed Defense Threshold, and the GM's own die for an adversary takes the typed number less 10. 342: a row's [CHECK ...] block is the word whatever its Constellation column and Effect say; a row with none keeps the build's guess. 343: the user picks first and the target answers knowing the pick. 344: nobody is asked when the target can use exactly one of the Defenses named. 345: a row that names one Defense reads it even when the target cannot use it, and the card says so (it used to be read against Awareness with nothing said). 346: nothing is paid until the roll; a request can be withdrawn before an answer, lapses with its Combat, gives one roll, and stands after the user's Opportunity has ended; an adversary pays when its request goes out. 347: the first valid answer card in the chat log stands, and an answer counts only from the target's owner or the GM. 348: an adversary's result is its own card, read from the player's roll, with the APPLY buttons the GM's. 349: the block is read on a Maneuver's own row alone.
recommendation: Leave them. The two to know are 345 (a Grabbed target is now read against Evade when the row says only Evade, where it used to be read against Awareness) and 346 (a request stands after the user's Opportunity has ended; say if it should lapse with that Opportunity instead).

where: data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx: Seek, Anticipate, Stabilize, Hide, Sneak; AUTOMATION_GRAMMAR.md, section 5, Declaring a check
question: The right side of vs reads a Defense or a number. Five rows are read against something else: Seek against the hider's Stealth, Anticipate against the foe's Guile, Stabilize against 10 + Dying + Wounds, Hide and Sneak against each watcher's Awareness. Their blocks can name what is rolled, and the Threshold is then typed.
recommendation: Paste the blocks that name what is rolled ([CHECK Awareness], [CHECK Insight], [CHECK Medicine], [CHECK Stealth]) and type the Threshold at the table. If a Constellation on the right of vs is wanted (the target's Stealth or Guile as a Threshold of 10 plus its bonus), say so and it is the next word after the Bind's.

where: foundry/starwrought/module/documents/actor/bind.mjs; data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx, the Gain Control row
question: Gain Control's check and its results are still code (0.27.0). With [CHECK Melee vs Guard] sayable since 0.34.0, what is missing is a word for what each degree does to the Bind (Controlling, neutral, the foe Controlling).
recommendation: Leave N/A in Gain Control's Automation cell for now. The next release gives the grammar one word for Bind results, and the row is then written as [CHECK Melee vs Guard] with one result line for each degree.

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.33.0, rulings 325, 327, 328, 329, 331, 332, 334, 335
question: Readings 0.33.0 makes that Mike did not rule on. 325: a Condition that includes another counts as it to every rule, once (a Prone creature is Off-Guard to IFT: EFFECT(off-guard), and REMOVE: off-guard does not stand it up). 327: a first Torso Wound and the Torso's Critical Hit effect count as Off-Guard through the Off-Guard row. 328: Off-Guard against X holds only against the creature that applied the Condition with a Maneuver; one toggled from the token names nobody. 329: the row is the word, so N/A on a row means the Condition changes no number (Off-Guard, Frightened and Fatigued included), and the system's old numbers for those three stand only when the workbook cannot be read. 331: an Off-Guard that comes from a Prone you applied counts as yours for `mine`. 332: Unconscious can still be applied by a Maneuver. 334: a Condition's lines have no On / Skip / Off. 335: an adversary's sheet shows the typed number in the field and the number in effect beside it, and a reroll meets the number the first die met.
recommendation: Leave them. The one to know is 329: emptying the Off-Guard, Frightened or Fatigued row's Automation cell switches that Condition's numbers off for everyone. Keep the lines unless that is what is wanted.

where: data/conditions.xlsx, the Prone and Supine rows; the Unconscious row's Includes
question: A creature that has two Conditions takes the lines of both. One that is both Prone and Supine takes -2 to attacks twice and +2 Evade against a ranged Blow twice. Drop Prone and Drop Supine each take the other off, so a Maneuver never leaves both, but an Unconscious creature (which counts as Prone) laid on its back, or both toggled from the token, has both. Also: Prone's line reads IFT: RANGED, which is a ranged Blow, so the +2 Evade does not reach a Blast thrown from range.
recommendation: Leave it and hold the edge at the table. If an Unconscious creature should be Supine and not Prone, change Unconscious's Includes cell. If the +2 Evade should also answer a ranged Blast, say so and the line gets a word for it.

where: data/conditions.xlsx, the Supine row's Automation cell
question: Supine's Effect says -2 Situation to Attacks 'except melee Attacks against adjacent creatures, Grapples included'. The grammar has no word for the exception, so the row's [EFFECT ATK: -2 situation] reaches those attacks too. Supine also does not stop movement yet (no word for what a Condition forbids).
recommendation: Keep the line for now and hold the exception at the table, or delete the ATK line from the Supine row until the exception has a word (then nothing is taken off a Supine creature's attacks). The words for what a Condition forbids are the next release, one at a time.

where: data/conditions.xlsx, the Prone row's Effect cell (copied from the handbook's Conditions table as written)
question: The Prone row ends 'Stand to clear, or Roll Over to become Prone.' Rolling over from Prone would make a creature Supine, so the last word reads like a slip. The same sentence is in the handbook's table.
recommendation: Change the last word to Supine in the Effect cell of data/conditions.xlsx and double-click sync_conditions.cmd. The handbook's table is yours to mend or to take out of the book.

where: Starwrought_Players_Handbook_v4.25.docx, the Conditions table; data/conditions.xlsx
question: data/conditions.xlsx is now the only source for a Condition, by Mike's answer. The handbook still prints its Conditions table, and nothing checks the two against each other, so they will drift as the sheet is edited.
recommendation: Replace the table in the handbook with the placeholder the equipment tables got ('This section will be populated from the Spreadsheets in the StarWrought data folder') when convenient. No redline is proposed for a Condition from now on.

where: data/equipment.xlsx, the Enabled? column of the Weapons sheet; the converter's warning each build
question: The saved equipment sheet enables one weapon, the Unarmed Strike. So the 0.30.0 equipment build took Dagger, Shortsword and Spear out of the Equipment pack (characters who hold one keep it), and Arrows, Bolts and Bullets ship with no weapon that takes them.
recommendation: If that was not meant, set Enabled? = Yes on the weapons that should be usable in Foundry (the three melee ones, and a bow or a crossbow to use the ammunition) and double-click sync_equipment.cmd.
decidedBy: Mike's sheet as saved after the 0.30.0 build: every row reads Yes (29 weapons, 27 armor, 3 shields, 3 ammunition). Built with the equipment build on 2026-11-17 and committed with 0.31.0

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.30.0, rulings 298 and 304
question: Two readings 0.30.0 makes that Mike did not rule on. 298: ammunition is taken when the weapon is loaded and never at the Strike (a weapon starts loaded, so a new bow's first shot costs no arrow), and with two kinds carried for one Weapon Group the stack In hand is used first, then by name. 304: Sync content refuses sources built for a newer system than the world is running, and says to restart Foundry.
recommendation: Leave both. Say so if a Strike should take the arrow instead of the Reload: it is one change, in loadWeapon's caller and the Strike's shot.

where: data/equipment.xlsx, the About sheet
question: The About sheet still says the workbook follows the Player's Handbook v4.10 Chapter 5 and that sheets other than Weapons, Armor and Shields are ignored. Since 2026-11-15 the handbook prints none of those tables and the workbook is their only source, and the Ammunition sheet is read.
recommendation: Reword the About sheet when convenient; nothing reads it.

where: assets/xlsx_to_trees.py (write_equipment), assets/app_template.html, assets/build_phb.js
question: The web app and the Constellation Compendium docx print the roster's four equipment blocks, so they list neither ammunition nor a ranged weapon's price (the ranged table has no price column, and the sheet now prices ranged weapons).
recommendation: Decide when the equipment is finalized: a fifth roster block for ammunition and a price column on the ranged table are a small change in the converter, the app and the docx builder.

where: module/documents/actor/carrying.mjs, loadWeapon (the one place a weapon is loaded); data/equipment.xlsx (no ammunition rows); PHB v4.25 Chapter 5 (no arrows, bolts or bullets printed)
question: 0.29.0 tracks whether a ranged weapon is loaded and Mike chose to count ammunition too, as its own step. The book and the data have no ammunition: no item, no price, no bundle size. So a Reload never runs out today.
recommendation: Plan it next, with four answers from Mike first: what the ammunition items are (arrows, bolts, sling bullets) and which weapon takes which; the bundle size and price; whether a Reload with none left is refused or warned (the empty weapon's rule is warn and go on); and whether a shot can be recovered after a fight. Then a gear row for each, a link from weapon to ammunition, and loadWeapon takes it from the pack.
decidedBy: Mike, 2026-11-15: he added the Ammunition tab to data/equipment.xlsx (Arrows, Bolts and Bullets, ten to a stack, 1 gp, by Weapon Group) and chose, by question, warn and go on with none left and recovery left to the table; built as 0.30.0 (rulings 298 to 300)

where: data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx, Basic Actions sheet, the Strike row's Automation cell; printed in foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md (0.29.0) and AUTOMATION_GRAMMAR.md section 5
question: Strike's conditions are a cell for Mike to paste: [REQUIRES foe in reach or ranged weapon loaded or weapon thrown] [REQUIRES foe in sight] [REQUIRES not restrained] [REQUIRES not unconscious]. Until the row carries it the Maneuvers tab always lists Strike. The [REQUIRES weapon reload] printed for Reload with 0.28.0 is withdrawn: Reload's condition is in code now.
recommendation: Paste the four blocks in place of the N/A and run sync_content.cmd. Do not paste the Reload block from the 0.28.0 list.

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.29.0, rulings 292, 293 and 294
question: Three readings 0.29.0 makes that Mike did not rule on. 292: Reload costs the weapon's own Reload N (the trait's "N Interact actions"), is Prepared at three, and costs nothing outside an encounter or with the six-action round untracked. 293: the count is corrected by a click on the chip at no cost. 294: with an Unarmed Strike always in hand, a character holding only a bow has a reach of 2 ft where the sheet read 0, so it counts for Support, draws a reach ring and is offered an Intercept as an unarmed Quick Strike; and the Unarmed Strike, being Finesse, always rolls Agility.
recommendation: Leave 292 and 293. On 294, say so if an archer with both hands on a bow should threaten nothing: the remedy would be a Two-Handed weapon in hand switching the fist off for reach and Intercept, which is one check in longestMelee's callers.

where: Starwrought_Players_Handbook_v4.25.docx, Chapter 5, Weapon Traits, Reload [N] (the text is in a table nested in the cell); data/maneuvers.xlsx, the Reload row
question: The Reload [N] trait says "After firing, you must spend N Interact actions before the weapon can fire again", while data/maneuvers.xlsx has a Reload Maneuver of its own (none to six actions). The system pays the Reload Maneuver at N. The two agree on the cost and differ on the name.
recommendation: One wording pass in Word when convenient: "you must Reload (N actions) before the weapon can fire again". The cell nests a table, which the redline tool will not edit, so it is a hand edit.
decidedBy: Mike, 2026-11-15: "The reload trait already does have words in the book"; the trait's wording stands and the system pays the Reload Maneuver at N, so nothing changes

where: data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx, the Automation cells of 28 rows; the blocks are printed in foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md (0.28.0) and AUTOMATION_GRAMMAR.md section 5
question: The Maneuvers tab lists only what applies now, and a Maneuver's own conditions are a [REQUIRES ...] block in its row's Automation cell. Until a row has its block the tab always lists it. Twenty-eight rows have a block written for them (Stand and Kip Up: [REQUIRES prone or supine]; Grapple: [REQUIRES free hand or weapon grapple][REQUIRES creature in reach]; and the rest), and three more are a judgement about how the table plays (Release, Sneak, Battle Cry).
recommendation: Paste the 28 in place of the N/A or empty cells and run sync_content.cmd; leave Release, Sneak and Battle Cry unwritten unless the table tracks what they ask (a Grab held with an empty hand, Hidden as a Condition on the token). Since 0.29.0 the Reload block of that list is withdrawn (Reload's condition is in code), so 27 remain; Strike's cell is its own row here.

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.28.0, rulings 283, 286, 287 and 289; module/rules/requires.mjs, module/helpers/situation.mjs
question: Four readings the Maneuvers tab makes that Mike did not rule on. 283: a row is left out only when the system KNOWS it does not apply (no token on the map, an unsure hand count and a Blinded character hide nothing). 286: a row with a Trigger and no Reaction mark in its Cost cell (Battle Cry, Sure Seat, Steady the Line) is kept on the list off-turn as a Reaction, though the engine still gates and charges it as a plain Maneuver. 287: who is near is every other token the character's own token can see, edge to edge, never one hidden from the players, a party token or a dead body; a free hand is an estimate. 289: nothing is refused (a dimmed row can be used), and an owned copy of a Basic Maneuver is listed in place of the Basic row.
recommendation: Leave all four. 286 goes away when the rows' Cost cells carry the Reaction mark, which also settles the open point of 0.23.0 for the engine.

where: Starwrought_Players_Handbook_v4.25.docx, four tracked changes by Claude (assets/phb_propose.py, PROPOSALS["bind"]); the file before them is in backup/pre-0.27.0/
question: Four tracked changes wait in the edition: under Binds, "A Quick Strike that is Stopped forms at most a neutral Bind." (ruling 272); under Ending a Bind, "A Cast is such an attack. A shield that holds the Control is the exception ..." (rulings 270 and 273); and the Conditions table's Bound [X] and Controlled [X] rows brought into line with Ending a Bind. Accept or reject each?
recommendation: Accept all four in Word and save; the next build reports the same-numbered file changed, and Claude compares it with the committed copy and records it again.
decidedBy: Mike, 2026-11-15: all four accepted in Word with nothing else changed (compared paragraph by paragraph with the committed file); recorded again with 0.29.0

where: System 0.27.0, rulings 276 and 280 (foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md)
question: Two rulings of 0.27.0 are Claude's readings, not Mike's answers. 276: a Strike that "resolves before the Bind ends" keeps the Zone the Control held open on its own result card, and the Bind ends before that card (a damage button may never be pressed). 280: Gain Control takes no -2 for a Controlled implement, and a fighter who already Controls cannot use it. Do they stand? (Ruling 277 is settled: Mike, 2026-11-19, "Keep as is". Close needs no click and is the Controller's Step alone; a Step closer by a fighter who is not Controlling ends the Bind.)
recommendation: Let both stand. 276 removes a decision with no cost; for 280, say so if a Controlled fighter's Gain Control should be the harder roll, and the -2 is one line.

where: module/documents/actor/bind.mjs (one Bind for each fighter); module/documents/actor/wounds.mjs, rigidImplement (a held shield before any weapon)
question: The book says "Track no more than one Bind per implement", so a fighter with a sword and a shield could hold two. The system holds one Bind for each fighter, and when a card forms it the implement is the shield if one is held. So a neutral Bind on the shield ends when its bearer Strikes with the sword, and a foe who Controls the shield puts no -2 on the sword. Is one Bind for each fighter enough, and should the defender choose which implement Guarded?
recommendation: Keep one Bind for each fighter until play asks for two. Add the implement choice to the card's Form a Bind and Take Control only if shield-bearers find the shield-first rule costs them; Form a Bind on the sheet already lets the player name the sword.

where: Gain Control (module/documents/actor/bind.mjs) and the other Maneuvers with the Attack trait that roll a check: Disarm, Grapple, Trip, Shove
question: A Maneuver with the Attack trait that rolls a check (Gain Control's Melee, Disarm's Athletics) takes none of the attacker's attack penalties today: an Arms Wound's -2 to attacks, Fatigued, the Arms' Critical Hit effect. An adversary's Gain Control does take the Arms' Critical Hit effect, since it reads the Attack Threshold. Should the Attack trait bring those penalties onto the check?
recommendation: Yes, as one rule for every Attack-trait check, decided once: it would make an injured arm matter in a grapple and in the Bind alike. Until then none applies, which is how every such Maneuver has always rolled.

where: module/rules/kinds/bonus.mjs, the Defense branch of a check; ruling 222 (0.21.0)
question: Ruling 222 lets a bonus to a Maneuver reach a check rolled with a Defense Constellation from that Maneuver's Item (Humanity's +1 on an Aid made with Awareness). Should a bonus to every check, and a bonus to a Maneuver made without its Item, also reach a Defense rolled as a check (Wind's Endure, a Recovery, a Search with Awareness)? Today neither does: nothing is applied and nothing is offered there. Since 0.36.0 (ruling 370) a bonus to EVERY ROLL, a bare CHECK, does reach a Defense rolled as a check, once, through the Defense's own number. What is still open is the narrow pair: a SKILL line, and a bonus to a Maneuver made without its Item.
recommendation: Half settled by 0.36.0. For the narrow pair: leave it unless a Talent wants a SKILL bonus on a Search made with Awareness; that would need SKILL to be counted on a check rolled with a Defense's Constellation.

where: module/rules/kinds/substitute.mjs, the third descriptor of USE; rulings 219 and 111
question: A USE line names a Maneuver's check and nothing wider (ruling 219); a Constellation there is refused ('a Constellation's own checks are not read yet'). When a Talent wants a Constellation as the check a USE names, does the swap carry into an Initiative rolled with that Constellation? Ruling 111 (an Initiative rolled with a Constellation carries every modifier of that Constellation's check) argues yes.
recommendation: Settle it with the first Talent that names one; the refusal stands until then.

where: data/talents_ancestries.xlsx, the Human sheet in progress (Mike's, uncommitted)
question: 16 Automation cells on the Human sheet hold only '# PROPOSED' notes naming tags the grammar does not have (ALTER, PREPARE, CONDITION and extra IF conditions), Jack of All Trades' and Quick Study's among them, so those Talents automate nothing once the sheet builds; and Torchbearer Human's cell no longer carries the Rally Aura. Which comes first?
recommendation: Pick the next kind from them with Claude, one at a time (ruling 119), from the Talent that wants it most; the others stay '#' notes, which the grammar reads as comments, until their kind exists. Cells that can be written today are printed in the 0.22.0, 0.24.0 and 0.25.0 changelog entries and in AUTOMATION_GRAMMAR.md section 5. Four are already on the saved sheets (Patient Assistance, Sure Assistance, Coordinated Footwork, Move Together's row). Three things wait: Aid's five GIVE lines on its row (0.22.0; its Automation cell is still empty, so no Aid gives a result), a ROW for Pay It Forward on the Ancestry Actions sheet (Cost 0, Frequency 'Once per encounter', text from the draft workbook) with '[EFFECT SUBORDINATE: Aid; IF: EFFECT(Aid, used); LIMIT: encounter]', and '[EFFECT ALTER: Pay It Forward.limit; VALUE: round]' on Reciprocal Effort (0.25.0).

where: PHB v4.25, Conditions table (Mike's final wording, 2026-11-15); data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx, Drop Prone, Stand, Kip Up and a Roll Over row to come
question: Supine is defined in the handbook's Conditions table: Off-Guard; -2 Situation to Attacks except melee against an adjacent creature (Grapples included); +2 Situation to Evade against ranged; no Move, Step, Rush, Leap or Crawl; Stand or Roll Over to clear. Mike did not take the sentence saying Supine is not Prone, so whether a rule that names Prone also means Supine is unsaid. The Prone row now ends "or Roll Over to become Prone", which reads like a slip for Supine. The system still has Prone alone (ruling 266).
recommendation: Mend the Prone row's last word in Word (Supine), add the Roll Over row (Cost 1, Traits Motion, Requirements "You are Prone or Supine.", Effect "Change from Prone to Supine, or from Supine to Prone.") and enable Drop Prone on the Basic Actions sheet, say whether a rule naming Prone reaches Supine, then have Supine built: a condition beside Prone, the attack penalty read against the gap to the target, the movement refusal in the drag, and Roll Over as a Maneuver the system implements.

where: data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx Cost cells: Battle Cry, Lost in the Dark, Reliable Anchor, Steady the Line, Sure Seat, Quick Tongue, No Quarter, Grab an Edge
question: These rows have a Trigger and no Reaction glyph in their Cost, so the system reads each as a plain Maneuver. Since 0.23.0 a plain Maneuver used from the sheet pays its cost, so the five that cost one action pay it from their row and wait for the GM off-turn (Quick Tongue pays from its card button; the two at nought pay nothing). The same is true of any row whose empty Cost cell reads as one action.
recommendation: Write the cost with its Reaction glyph in each Cost cell (Battle Cry is nought with the glyph in the book). A Reaction is paid the moment it is used and never waits for the GM.

Step two is his Fantasy Grounds idea in full: a Maneuver puts a named Effect on its target for a duration, and CHECK, DEF and ATK lines apply IF: EFFECT(<name>) on the owner or IFT: EFFECT(<name>) on the other party.

where: data/talents_magic.xlsx (the Targets column is prose); module/canvas/area-targets.mjs; PHB v4.25, Area Attacks
question: 0.26.0 aims an area and rules none of it: a template you draw targets what is inside, and the attack rolls once for each target. The book's own clauses wait for data: "Unless the Talent specifies otherwise" (no Talent can ask for one roll for all), a spell's own shape and size, and "an area Attack does not automatically gain these location-specific effects" (the system cannot tell an area Attack from another, so its Critical Hit effect is the GM's to switch off).
recommendation: Plan it on its own when the first area spell is authored: two columns on the spell rows (Area: shape and size; Rolls: each or one), the Cast placing the template and removing it when the attack ends, and the Critical Hit effect withheld for an attack that came from one.

where: v4.25-sync-report.md, rulings 256 and 260
question: Two readings the sync made that the book does not settle. 256: two overlapping Difficult regions of the SAME kind are two effects (x3), as two of different kinds are. 260: every Critical Hit that does damage sets its Zone's effect, an area Attack's included, and the Zone's switch on the sheet is the GM's remedy.
recommendation: Leave both unless play says otherwise; 256 is the one most likely to be argued (one circumstance counted once would make two mud regions x2).

where: foundry/starwrought/CHANGELOG.md, 0.32.0, rulings 313 to 318, 320 and 321
question: Readings 0.32.0 made so that APPLY and REMOVE could be built. 313: a Condition already on by other means (the GM's hand, a Critical Hit, a Bind) is left alone, nothing added and nothing taken off by a window. 314: of two APPLYs of one Effect the later window stands. 315: Dropping Prone by choice is not stopped by an IMMUNE line and does not use it up; a Prone by a Trip's result is. 316: an Effect with a window is put on only in an encounter the user or the recipient is fighting in. 317: frightened 2 on a creature already Frightened 3 changes nothing. 318: outside an encounter a row with a range of costs asks which version this use is. 320: an applied named Effect shows on everyone's hover card. 321: APPLY on a target needs IF: RESULT, and a row the system runs another way (Strike, Rush's drag) applies nothing.
recommendation: Leave them unless play says otherwise. The two most likely to be argued are 313 (a Demoralize does nothing to a creature the GM already made Frightened by hand at a lower value: it raises it, but puts no window on it) and 321 (Rush's Off-Guard is still by hand).

where: data/actions_maneuvers.xlsx (Talk Them Down, Anticipate, Bolster, Feint, Tumble Through); AUTOMATION_GRAMMAR.md section 5, Putting Effects on
question: APPLY puts an Effect on a creature, but a Basic Maneuver's row cannot make that Effect DO anything for everyone: 'it takes -2 to its next Attack against you' needs a line on the creature that reads the Effect, and such a line lives on a Talent or an owned Maneuver. The same gap leaves the Wrong-Footed Condition's own effect (Off-Guard against that creature only) to the table, though Feint now records who Wrong-Footed whom.
recommendation: Plan it as the next step in two parts. First the small one: treat Wrong-Footed applied by X as Off-Guard against X in the Defense read, since the record now says who. Then an Effect that carries its own lines, written on the APPLY line's row, so Talk Them Down and Anticipate can be automated from a Basic row.

where: module/rules/kinds/bonus.mjs; module/config/modifiers.mjs (resolveModifiers); found by the review of 0.36.0
question: One Talent or Condition counts once on a roll, the stronger of its lines. A line that is set aside still uses up what it carries: a LIMIT (once a round, once an encounter) is counted as used, and a ticked claim that is weaker than a standing line of the same Talent is spent for nothing. And an every-roll line that asks about the roll's own rank (IF: RANK(roll ...)) reaches no Defense: the build warns. No cell on the sheets does either today.
recommendation: Leave both until a Talent runs into one. Write SKILL for a roll-rank bonus that is about checks (Jack of All Trades).
